name: Quantitative Saliency Benchmark
description: Saliency Maps (SMs) have been extensively used to interpret deep learning models decision by highlighting the features deemed relevant by the model. They are used on highly nonlinear problems, where linear feature selection (FS) methods fail at highlighting relevant explanatory variables. However, the reliability of gradient-based feature attribution methods such as SM has mostly been only qualitatively (visually) assessed, and quantitative benchmarks are currently missing, partially due to the lack of a definite ground truth on image data. Concerned about the apophenic biases introduced by visual assessment of these methods, in this paper we propose a synthetic quantitative benchmark for Neural Networks (NNs) interpretation methods. For this purpose, we built synthetic datasets with nonlinearly separable classes and increasing number of decoy (random) features, illustrating the challenge of FS in high-dimensional settings. We also compare these methods to conventional approaches such as mRMR or Random Forests. Our results show that our simple synthetic datasets are sufficient to challenge most of the benchmarked methods. TreeShap, mRMR and LassoNet are the best performing FS methods. We also show that, when quantifying the relevance of a few non linearly-entangled predictive features diluted in a large number of irrelevant noisy variables, neural network-based FS and interpretation methods are still far from being reliable.
general_score_metric: precision@k (average precision in identifying true predictive features)
reputation: A niche academic benchmark for quantitative evaluation of saliency/feature-attribution methods on synthetic data; primarily cited within interpretability and feature-selection research.
notes: Synthetic, non-LLM benchmark focused on feature-selection in controlled settings; small-scale and may not transfer directly to real-world image interpretability. Evaluations focus on identifying ground-truth predictive features rather than natural-image saliency.
